  'status': 'complete',
  'statement': 'For every type ι, positive natural number n, real-valued array x indexed by {0,…,n−1} × ι, nonnegative real u, and real error array δ indexed by ℕ × ℕ × ι, the specified reduction has a componentwise backward-error representation if its active additions have |δ| ≤ u and d u < 1, where d is the ceiling base-2 logarithm of n. The reduction repeatedly pairs positions k and k + ceil(n/2"'^(ℓ+1)) of the previous stage, multiplies each paired sum by 1 + δ(ℓ,k,c), and copies any unpaired position unchanged. Its output is position 0 after d stages. The theorem asserts that this output is the exact sum of some perturbed input arrays with |Δx(i,c)| ≤ (d u)/(1−d u) |x(i,c)|. The separately defined coefficients track the weights of the original inputs in this actual recurrence; backwardPerturbation multiplies each original input by its final coefficient minus one. The target statement quantifies existentially over perturbations and does not explicitly identify its witness with backwardPerturbation.'"',
  'targets': [{
    'name': p + 'parallel_binary_tree_reduction',
    'statement': 'For every type ι (at any universe level), every n ∈ ℕ with 0 < n, every x : Fin n → (ι → ℝ), every u ∈ ℝ with 0 ≤ u, and every δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ, assume LocalRoundingModel(n,u,δ) and (d : ℝ)u < 1, where d = depth(n). Then there exists Δx : Fin n → (ι → ℝ) such that computed(x,δ) = ∑_{i∈Fin n}(x(i) + Δx(i)) as functions ι → ℝ, and for every i ∈ Fin n and every c ∈ ι, |Δx(i,c)| ≤ gamma(d,u)|x(i,c)| = ((d : ℝ)u/(1−(d : ℝ)u))|x(i,c)|. Equivalently the equality holds at every c: stage(x,δ,d,0,c) = ∑_{i=0}"'^{n−1}(x(i,c)+Δx(i,c)). Here Fin n denotes the natural indices 0 ≤ i < n; addition and the finite sum of functions are pointwise. LocalRoundingModel is exactly the active-pair bound specified below; no bounds on unused δ entries are required. The output is the particular stage recurrence below, not an arbitrary summation procedure. The separately defined backwardPerturbation is the coefficient-based perturbation associated with that recurrence, but its name does not occur in this theorem statement.'"'
  }],
  'constructions': [
    {'name': p+'depth', 'description': 'For every n ∈ ℕ, depth(n) = Nat.clog(2,n), the natural ceiling base-2 logarithm: 0 when n = 0, and the least d ∈ ℕ for which n ≤ 2"'^d when n > 0. In particular depth(1) = 0. This is the stage index used by computed and backwardPerturbation and the factor in the theorem’s smallness hypothesis and error bound.'"'},
    {'name': p+'stageSize', 'description': 'For all n,ℓ ∈ ℕ, put s_ℓ = stageSize(n,ℓ) = floor((n + 2"'^ℓ − 1)/2''^ℓ) = ceil(n/2''^ℓ). The displayed subtraction and division are natural-number subtraction (truncated at zero) and natural-number division; 2''^ℓ is always positive, so the numerator here is nonnegative without truncation. Thus s_0 = n and stageSize(0,ℓ) = 0. These sizes determine the surviving positions and the pairing offsets at every stage.'"'},
    {'name': p+'gamma', 'description': 'For every k ∈ ℕ and u ∈ ℝ, gamma(k,u) = ((k : ℝ)u)/(1−(k : ℝ)u). This definition has no positivity or nonzero-denominator hypotheses; real division in Lean is total, with division by zero equal to zero. In the target it is used only with k = depth(n), 0 ≤ u, and k u < 1, so its denominator is strictly positive.'},
    {'name': p+'stage', 'description': 'For every type ι, n ∈ ℕ, x : Fin n → ι → ℝ, and δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ, define S_ℓ(k,c) = stage(x,δ,ℓ,k,c) for all ℓ,k ∈ ℕ and c ∈ ι. Set S_0(k,c) = x(⟨k,k<n⟩,c) if k < n, and 0 otherwise. For each ℓ ∈ ℕ set m = stageSize(n,ℓ+1) and s = stageSize(n,ℓ). If k ≥ m, set S_{ℓ+1}(k,c) = 0. If k < m and k+m < s, set S_{ℓ+1}(k,c) = (S_ℓ(k,c)+S_ℓ(k+m,c))(1+δ(ℓ,k,c)). If k < m and k+m ≥ s, set S_{ℓ+1}(k,c) = S_ℓ(k,c). Thus each new active position pairs the corresponding position in the first portion with the position offset by m, when present; an unpaired entry is copied without any δ factor. Pairing is by this offset, rather than by consecutive indices 2k and 2k+1. All these operations are exact real operations with the specified multiplicative factors; no machine arithmetic, execution schedule, or stochastic error mechanism is defined. The recurrence is defined at every natural stage, including stages beyond depth(n), and requires no rounding bound to be defined.'},
    {'name': p+'computed', 'description': 'For every type ι, n ∈ ℕ, x : Fin n → ι → ℝ and δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ, computed(x,δ) is the function c ↦ stage(x,δ,depth(n),0,c). For n > 0 the active size at that final stage is one. For n = 0 the defined output is the zero function; the target excludes this case. For n = 1 it returns x(0,c) with no addition or error factor.'},
    {'name': p+'LocalRoundingModel', 'description': 'For every type ι, n ∈ ℕ, u ∈ ℝ and δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ, LocalRoundingModel(n,u,δ) is the proposition: for every ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ < depth(n), every k ∈ ℕ with k < stageSize(n,ℓ+1) and k + stageSize(n,ℓ+1) < stageSize(n,ℓ), and every c ∈ ι, |δ(ℓ,k,c)| ≤ u. It bounds precisely the factors used in actual paired additions before the output stage. It imposes no bound on unpaired positions, inactive positions, or stages at or beyond depth(n), and does not itself include 0 ≤ u. It is vacuous when there are no such pairs.'},
    {'name': p+'coefficient', 'description': 'For every type ι, n ∈ ℕ and δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ, define A_ℓ(k,i,c) = coefficient(δ,ℓ,k,i,c) for ℓ,k ∈ ℕ, i ∈ Fin n and c ∈ ι.
